triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale carries an inventory FILE NAME in row prose - '(psalm_device_inventory.json: Ps 64 yhwh=1, elohim=3; Ps 60-65 together carry 1 yhwh against 22 elohim, Elohistic-Psalter texture)' - which the book's register law bars (row prose describes the TEXT, never the process; cross-row references verse-anchored). E-18 arm, re-derived from the staged OSHB bytes with the skeleton sweep: the Tetragrammaton stands in exactly 1 verse and 1 token of Psalm 64, at oshb:Ps.64.11 (= web:Ps.64.10, the row's own closing verse); the full spelling of Elohim stands in 3 verses / 3 tokens of Psalm 64; across Ps 60-65 the Tetragrammaton stands in 1 verse / 1 token and Elohim in 19 verses / 22 tokens. The substantive claim is TRUE, so this is a register defect at low severity, not an evidence defect - but see the separate count-unit finding on the 22.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale cites an inventory by file name inside row prose.
findings.grounds: The string 'psalm_device_inventory.json' stands twice-over in the row's driver field and once more, as 'device inventory count: 1', in observed_substrate_signals[1]; the book's register law (row prose describes the text, not the process) admits no tooling names. The counts the citation carries re-derive TRUE from bytes (Tetragrammaton 1 verse / 1 token in Psalm 64 at oshb:Ps.64.11 = web:Ps.64.10; Elohim, full spelling, 3 verses / 3 tokens), so nothing but the register is at fault.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace the parenthetical with a verse-anchored, unit-named form, e.g. 'Yahweh stands in 1 verse of Psalm 64, at oshb:Ps.64.11 (skeleton tier), against Elohim in 3 verses' - no file name in row prose. No span, seam or confidence change.

findings.claim: The Ps 60-65 divine-name digits name no count unit, and the unit changes the digit: 22 is the Elohim TOKEN count, while the verse count is 19.

The row writes '1 yhwh against 22 elohim' with no unit word, so the figure is only true read as tokens; the book's law requires every universal/comparative digit to name its unit (verses vs occurrences). Pure texture in this row - the seam does not rest on it.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale names an inventory file in row prose: 'the consecutive le-David run recorded in psalm_device_inventory.json across Ps 51-65 (15/15 psalms)'. E-18 arm, re-derived from bytes: sweeping the le-David label at skeleton tier over each psalm's own MT title verse(s) (ps_lib.title_mt_refs, which returns MT vv1-2 for the four shift+2 psalms 51/52/54/60 and MT v1 elsewhere) returns a hit in all fifteen psalms 51-65, and NO hit in the flanking psalms 50, 66 and 67 - so the run is both 15/15 and maximal at both ends. The claim is TRUE and carries its digit with its unit ('15/15 psalms'); the defect is the file name alone, low severity.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale cites an inventory by file name inside row prose.

findings.claim: Confidence 'high' overstates a front seam whose only stated driver is a tense/topic pivot, with second-person address to God running unbroken across the seam.
findings.grounds: The row's front seam is web:Ps.65.8|web:Ps.65.9 (= oshb:Ps.65.9|oshb:Ps.65.10). Its sole stated driver is 'A tense/topic pivot', the 2ms perfect פָּקַ֥דְתָּ (oshb:Ps.65.10, byte tier). The book's tier-1 seam evidence is superscriptions, hallelu-Yah/hodu frames, doxologies, acrostic structure and explicit speaker/addressee shifts inside psalms; no addressee shift stands at this seam - oshb:Ps.65.9 already carries a 2ms suffix, מֵאוֹתֹתֶ֑יךָ (byte tier), and web:Ps.65.8 reads in WEB 'They also who dwell in faraway places are afraid at your wonders. You call the morning's dawn and the evening with songs of joy.' The seam-pair row discloses the same continuity from its own side. Psalm 65 carries no Selah (0 verses, byte sweep) and no marks-layer object at the seam, so no tier-3 corroboration is available either. Comparable content-pivot seams inside this batch ship at medium (M8-Ps-205, M8-Ps-208). The span itself is sound - the psalm closes at web:Ps.65.13, a ruled boundary - so this is a label disagreement, not a respan.
findings.proposed_change: Review confidence high -> medium, or add an independent tier-1 warrant for the web:Ps.65.8|web:Ps.65.9 seam. No respan proposed; routed onward as a disagreement with the row's own stated grounds.

triggers.grounds: The medium_low band is warranted and its stated reason is byte-honest. Front seam web:Ps.68.6|web:Ps.68.7 rests on a tier-1 vocative opening at oshb:Ps.68.8 corroborated by the Selah that closes the same verse (WEB 'God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah.'; MT 68:8 carries the selah word - 1 of the 3 selah verses of Psalm 68, at MT 68:8, 68:20 and 68:33, and the only one inside this span, so the span-scoped disclosure is complete). The stated reason for the low band - that the interior web:Ps.68.9-web:Ps.68.14 resists a finer tier-1 split and that the home-waiting figure, the silver dove and Zalmon snow are commentary-tradition cruxes - re-derives true: no imperative, vocative or addressee shift stands inside oshb:Ps.68.10-oshb:Ps.68.15, and the strategy registers Psalm 68 as an expected low-confidence region. The row also discloses rather than adopts its strongest rival, which is the honest posture at this band. The band is therefore sound; it is NOT, however, a cure for the two separate evidence defects recorded below, neither of which the band's stated reason covers.

findings.claim: The token denominator in the rejected-alternative digit is byte-false, and by exactly one verse of the shift+1 offset: web:Ps.68.11 has 6 tokens, not 7.
findings.grounds: The row writes '0 of 7 tokens there carry 2ms forms' of web:Ps.68.11. Psalm 68 is shift+1, so web:Ps.68.11 = oshb:Ps.68.12, whose staged (maqaf-free) text is אֲדֹנָ֥י יִתֶּן אֹ֑מֶר הַֽ֝מְבַשְּׂר֗וֹת צָבָ֥א רָֽב - SIX tokens. Seven is the token count of oshb:Ps.68.11, חַיָּתְךָ֥ יָֽשְׁבוּ בָ֑הּ תָּ֤כִ֥ין בְּטוֹבָתְךָ֖ לֶעָנִ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים, which is web:Ps.68.10 - the verse before. The claim is an original-language token claim in a non-identity psalm written against a bare web: ref with no oshb: dual-cite, exactly the hazard the dual-cite law exists to close. The substantive half is TRUE (no 2ms form stands in oshb:Ps.68.12), and the companion digit is TRUE as well: of the four preceding WEB verses 68:7-68:10 (= oshb:Ps.68.8-68.11), three carry 2ms forms - oshb:Ps.68.8, oshb:Ps.68.10 and oshb:Ps.68.11 - and oshb:Ps.68.9 does not. Only the denominator is wrong.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: '0 of 6 tokens there carry 2ms forms (web:Ps.68.11 = oshb:Ps.68.12), against 3 of the preceding 4 verses (web:Ps.68.7-web:Ps.68.10 = oshb:Ps.68.8-oshb:Ps.68.11)' - the original-language claim dual-cited.

findings.claim: The back-seam warrant locates a direct address at web:Ps.68.15 that the bytes place one verse later; the neighbor row states the correction explicitly.
findings.grounds: The row bounds the strophe by 'the vocative-plus-Selah opening at web:Ps.68.7 and the scene shift to direct address of the Bashan mountains at web:Ps.68.15'. web:Ps.68.15 = oshb:Ps.68.16, whose whole text is הַר אֱ֭לֹהִים הַר בָּשָׁ֑ן הַ֥ר גַּ֝בְנֻנִּ֗ים הַר בָּשָֽׁן - a verbless third-person noun chain with no second-person form of any kind (WEB: 'The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged.'). Direct address opens one verse later, at web:Ps.68.16 = oshb:Ps.68.17, on the 2mp verb plus vocative לָ֤מָּה תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮ ('Why do you look in envy, you rugged mountains'). The embedded neighbor row M8-Ps-192 argues the identical point against this row's wording - 'web:Ps.68.15's anaphoric mountain description is a verbless 3rd-person noun chain; the tier-1 vocative-shift opener is the direct address beginning at web:Ps.68.16' - so the seam is argued incompatibly across the pair. The seam LOCATION survives: oshb:Ps.68.16 opens fresh scene material and the neighbor row places its own front edge at the same verse; what fails is the tier-1 qualifier attached to it, which is the half doing the boundary work.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only, installed on this row (the seam-pair partner already reads correctly): re-cut the back-seam warrant to 'the scene shift at web:Ps.68.15 (= oshb:Ps.68.16), a verbless third-person mountain chain, with the tier-1 vocative shift following at web:Ps.68.16 (= oshb:Ps.68.17)'. No respan proposed; routed onward as a disagreement with the row's own stated grounds.

findings.claim: The 'does not repeat elsewhere' claim about the battle-report vocabulary carries no digit-bearing sweep count.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals[2] asserts that the plunder / dove-wings / Zalmon-snow terms 'draw on terms this psalm does not repeat elsewhere in its own bounds' with no adjacent count. Re-swept at skeleton tier across all 36 MT verses of Psalm 68, each named term stands in exactly 1 verse: plunder at oshb:Ps.68.13 (= web:Ps.68.12), dove and wing at oshb:Ps.68.14 (= web:Ps.68.13), Zalmon at oshb:Ps.68.15 (= web:Ps.68.14). The claim is TRUE as scoped to the three named terms; it simply ships without its digit and unit. (Silver, which the verse also carries, does recur at oshb:Ps.68.31 = web:Ps.68.30 - outside the three named terms, but a reason to keep the scope explicit.)
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: '...terms each standing in exactly 1 verse of Psalm 68 (skeleton tier, book-scoped sweep)'; keep the scope to the named terms.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale names an inventory file in row prose: 'Psalm 71 carries no title (1 of 34 title-less psalms in the book, per psalm_device_inventory.json)'. E-18 arm, re-derived from the staged offset map: 116 of the 150 psalms carry a WEB title, so 34 carry none, and Psalm 71 is one of them (no Ps.71.0 entry exists in verse_map_web.json; the psalm's rule is identity). The claim is TRUE and carries its digit; the defect is the file name alone, low severity.

boundary_rationale locates a recurrence by row position rather than by verse: the refuge form at oshb:Ps.71.7 'inside the following row's span'. The book's register law requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. E-18 arm, re-derived: the refuge root sweeps at skeleton tier to exactly two verses of Psalm 71 - oshb:Ps.71.1 and oshb:Ps.71.7, one token each, with no other consonantal collision anywhere in the psalm - so 'recurs once more in Psalm 71' is TRUE; and oshb:Ps.71.7 (= web:Ps.71.7, identity psalm) does fall inside M8-Ps-205's span Ps.71.5-Ps.71.8. A true claim merely phrased in workflow register: low.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale anchors a cross-row reference by row position ('inside the following row's span') instead of by verse.
findings.grounds: The refuge bracket is real and byte-true (skeleton sweep: the root stands in oshb:Ps.71.1 and oshb:Ps.71.7 only, one token each) and the row honestly disclaims it as a driver; the defect is the workflow phrasing, which the book's law replaces with a verse anchor. The Hebrew splices themselves re-collate byte tier at their cited refs, and the Psalm 31 comparison is exemplary - the fortress clause of oshb:Ps.71.3 matches oshb:Ps.31.4 at SKELETON tier only, and the row says 'skeleton tier' and dual-cites web:Ps.31.3 = oshb:Ps.31.4 correctly, with no byte/verbatim overclaim.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: '...recurs once more in Psalm 71, at oshb:Ps.71.7 (= web:Ps.71.7), across this row's own closing seam web:Ps.71.4|web:Ps.71.5' - verse-anchored, no row-position reference.

A true claim in workflow register: low. The reasoning it supports is a credit to the row - it refuses to let the particle carry the seam.

findings.claim: Two fields anchor the same cross-row reference by row position instead of by verse.
findings.grounds: Both occurrences ('the following row's own strophe'; 'inside the following row's own span') name a row by position where the book's law requires a verse anchor. Everything the phrase supports checks out: verse-initial causal particle at oshb:Ps.71.5 and oshb:Ps.71.10 only; the Psalm 22 parallel is quoted verbatim from WEB and dual-cited correctly (web:Ps.22.9 = oshb:Ps.22.10, web:Ps.22.10 = oshb:Ps.22.11, both arithmetically right for a shift+1 psalm - the quote-checker's neighbor-only note on that pair is the ordinary edge-crossing case, the row having written the range explicitly); and Psalm 71 carries no Selah (0 verses) so no disclosure is owed. Confidence medium is well matched to a seam the row itself declines to rest on the particle.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only, one edit installed in both fields: '...recurs verse-initially at oshb:Ps.71.10 (= web:Ps.71.10), inside the material beyond this row's closing seam web:Ps.71.8|web:Ps.71.9' - verse-anchored.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale carries the inventory name and its key in row prose: "pmarks_Ps.json kq['Ps.71.20']=2". The digit is TRUE - the staged marks inventory records the value 2 at MT key Ps.71.20, within a K/Q layer of 68 notes across 65 verses - and the row is right to disclose a K/Q crossing inside a quoted verse, so this is a register defect at low severity, not an evidence defect. The bytes bear the disclosure out: oshb:Ps.71.20 carries ketiv+qere adjacent at two places, הראיתנו הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי and תחיינו תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי, each a 1cp ketiv against a 1cs qere.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale carries an inventory file name and a raw inventory key in row prose.
findings.grounds: "pmarks_Ps.json kq['Ps.71.20']=2" is tooling register inside the driver field. The value re-derives TRUE from the staged inventory (kq['Ps.71.20'] = 2; layer totals 68 notes / 65 verses), and the underlying disclosure is correct, so nothing but the register is at fault.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: '...carries two ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Ps.71.20 (single-witness marks layer)' - the object named, no file name and no inventory key.

findings.claim: The K/Q disclosure is attached to a WEB 'us' that the ketiv/qere layer does not in fact fork.
findings.grounds: The row quotes 'bring us up again from the depths of the earth' (web:Ps.71.20) and explains 'this verse's finite verbs carry ketiv/qere person forks between 1cp and 1cs ... so its WEB "us" is a rendering choice rather than a settled MT plural'. The two forks stand elsewhere in the verse: הראיתנו הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי (ketiv 1cp / qere 1cs) and תחיינו תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי (ketiv 1cp / qere 1cs). The verb behind the quoted clause is תַּעֲלֵֽנִי, an unambiguous 1cs form carrying NO K/Q note - so that particular 'us' is a free rendering, not a forked reading, and 'this verse's finite verbs' overstates a 2-of-5 distribution. The conclusion the row draws (the WEB plural is not a settled MT plural) survives, and it is strengthened, not weakened, by the correction; only the attribution is loose.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: '...web:Ps.71.20 carries two ketiv/qere person forks, 1cp ketiv against 1cs qere, at oshb:Ps.71.20 (single-witness marks layer); the verse's closing verb is 1cs with no note, so the WEB plural in "bring us up again" is a rendering choice rather than a settled MT plural'.

triggers.grounds: Both driver fields anchor the neighbour by row position: boundary_rationale's 'turns from the petition register of the preceding row' and strongest_rejected_alternative's 'it belongs with the preceding row's God-directed address block'. The book's law requires verse-anchored cross-row references. E-18 arm, re-derived from bytes and all TRUE: oshb:Ps.76.11 (= web:Ps.76.10) closes on the 2ms-suffixed verb the row quotes (byte tier at its cited ref), oshb:Ps.76.12 (= web:Ps.76.11) opens on the two 2mp imperatives (byte tier), oshb:Ps.76.13 (= web:Ps.76.12) returns to third-person report, and the psalm's opening report register at oshb:Ps.76.2 (= web:Ps.76.1) is what it closes on. The exclusivity claim in the same field is a model of the form: 'Yahweh (skeleton tier) occurs in 1 verse of Psalm 76, prefixed as ... at oshb:Ps.76.12 (web:Ps.76.11)' re-sweeps TRUE at exactly 1 verse / 1 token, with the tier, the unit and the digit all named. True claims in workflow register: low.

findings.grounds: 'the preceding row' appears in boundary_rationale and again in strongest_rejected_alternative. Every substantive claim around it re-derives true (2ms suffix closing oshb:Ps.76.11; 2mp imperatives opening oshb:Ps.76.12; third-person close at oshb:Ps.76.13; 1 Yahweh verse in Psalm 76), and the seam-pair partner M8-Ps-231 argues the identical seam from its own side with the same byte evidence - a coherent pair. Psalm 76's two Selah verses (oshb:Ps.76.4 and oshb:Ps.76.10 = web:Ps.76.3 and web:Ps.76.9) both fall outside this row's span-relevant set and are disclosed by that partner row, so no disclosure is owed here.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only, one edit installed in both fields: replace 'the preceding row' with the verse anchor, e.g. 'turns from the God-directed address that closes at web:Ps.76.10 (oshb:Ps.76.11)'.

findings.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative narrates a repair of the corpus's own earlier reading.
findings.grounds: 'Opening this row at web:Ps.76.10 (oshb:Ps.76.11), as the corpus previously read it, is rejected' - erratum narration, which the book's register law bars from row prose alongside decision ids, positional references and file-order talk. The rival and its rejection are otherwise sound and byte-grounded, so the clause can simply be dropped without touching the argument.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: delete 'as the corpus previously read it,' - the sentence stands unchanged otherwise.

triggers.grounds: The rival's rejection rests on a tier-4 English-sentence fact as its ONLY stated ground: 'A break after web:Ps.78.4's transmission pledge was considered but rejected because the purpose clauses of web:Ps.78.5-web:Ps.78.7 continue the same sentence movement toward the negative paradigm at web:Ps.78.8.' Translation punctuation and WEB sentence facts are never boundary evidence and never counterevidence by absence. This is driver work, not disclosure, so the lane confirms; and the cited layer does not even reach the seam the rival names - see the finding.

findings.claim: The rival's rejection rests solely on a WEB sentence-layer fact, and at that layer the WEB places a full stop exactly where the rival proposes the break.
findings.grounds: Read in the WEB itself, web:Ps.78.4 closes 'and his wondrous deeds that he has done.' with a period, and web:Ps.78.5 opens a fresh sentence 'For he established a covenant in Jacob...' that runs on through the semicolon and commas of web:Ps.78.6 and web:Ps.78.7 to the period closing web:Ps.78.8. So 'the same sentence movement' describes only the material AFTER the proposed seam: taken at the layer it cites, the argument shows that web:Ps.78.5-web:Ps.78.8 hang together, which is not a reason to reject a break at web:Ps.78.4|web:Ps.78.5 - the layer's own punctuation cuts the other way there. A tier-1 ground was available and unused: Psalm 78 is identity-numbered, and oshb:Ps.78.5 opens on the wayyiqtol וַיָּ֤קֶם (byte tier), a narrative continuation of oshb:Ps.78.4, which is what actually closes the proposed seam. The row's own observed_substrate_signals already carry byte-tier warrants for the chain that follows - לְמַ֤עַן at oshb:Ps.78.6 and וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ at oshb:Ps.78.7 - so the repair is a re-grounding, not new research. The row's real seams are untouched: its front edge is the psalm opening with its maskil superscription (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1, dual-cited by law, correctly called a superscription since this is a title and not a Ps 119 letter header), and its back edge at web:Ps.78.8|web:Ps.78.9 rests on the tribal naming at oshb:Ps.78.9.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-ground the rejection on the bytes - 'rejected because oshb:Ps.78.5 opens on a wayyiqtol continuing the narration of oshb:Ps.78.4, and the purpose-clause chain then runs from oshb:Ps.78.6 to the negative exemplar at oshb:Ps.78.8' - with no appeal to WEB sentence or punctuation facts. No respan proposed; the span survives on the re-grounded warrant.

findings.claim: The back-seam signal carries an unquantified 'unlike any' universal whose comparator is contestable.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals[2] reads 'a subject change unlike any within web:Ps.78.1-web:Ps.78.8', with no digit-bearing sweep count and no count object. Re-read against the bytes, the span does contain a subject change of comparable magnitude: after the first-person exordium of oshb:Ps.78.1-oshb:Ps.78.4 (1cs, then 1cp), oshb:Ps.78.5 turns to God as subject on וַיָּ֤קֶם, before the third-person plural of oshb:Ps.78.6-oshb:Ps.78.8. The seam at web:Ps.78.8|web:Ps.78.9 stands on its own facts - a generic collective given a tribal name at oshb:Ps.78.9, argued independently by the neighbour row - so the overclaim is in the comparative, not in the boundary.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: state the change without the universal, e.g. 'web:Ps.78.8's unnamed collective is specified by tribal name at oshb:Ps.78.9, the span's only shift from a generic to a named subject', or carry a digit-bearing count for whatever comparison is intended.
